p:cNvPr.descr: An illustration showing factors that affect the actvity of enzymes. On the left side of the illustration, it begins with (1) extracellular signals, with an arrow pointing to the receptor. There is also a small orange circle on the right of the receptor pointing down to another small orange circle, which has an arrow that points down and to the left to join with a transcription factor. Both of these point to a blue circle illustrating the (2) transcription of specific gene(s). In that cirlce, it shows the nucleus, with DNA binding to mRNA. Below that is a wavy green line representing mRNA, with an arrow pointing to those green lines broken up, representing (3) mRNA degradation. Below that is the wavy green line, with three ribosomes connected. The first has a small, light blue circular line at the bottom; the second has a longer circular blue line; and the third has the longest circular line, representing (4) mRNA translation on ribosome. On the right side of the illustration, in the middle, is a blue oval, entitled enzyme, with a single arrow pointing down to light blue triangular pieces, which represent (5) protein degradation (ubiquitin; proteasome). To the bottom right, a single arrow points to a rounded blue box entitled Endoplasmic reticulum, with a oval light blue circle inside, representing an (6) enzyme sequestered in subcellular organelle. Above that is an arrow pointing to a blue oval circle with a yellow "S" inside a small circle on the right line of the oval, which represents (7) enzyme binds substrate. The arrow has the small yellow "S" in the middle. From that oval, there is an arrow pointing back to the enzyme oval in the middle, with another arrow in the middle pointing down to "product." The enzyme in the middle then points to a square blue box with an L in a red circle at the bottom (ligand), which represents (8) enzyme binds ligand (allosteric effector). There is an arrow pointing back to the enzyme in the middle. On both arrows there is the red L circle. The enzyme in the middle then points to a small blue oval with a "P" in a small white circle attached to the circle on the outside, representing the enzyme undergoing phosphorylation/dephosphorylation. The line pointing has "kinase" written next to it. There is an arrow pointing back to the middle enzyme, with "phosphatase" written to the right. The middle enzyme then points to a small blue oval with a half light red circle attached at the bottom (regulatory protein), which shows (10) the enzyme combines with regulatory protein. It also points back to the enzyme in the middle. Both arrows have regulatory protein shooting off them.
